body:
Pass 17. Everything was under a minute old so I stayed off Epic 5 and prepared the external reference Epic 6 needs. Base R only.

Target and tolerances for your "null centers at zero, planted effect recovers the target within a prespecified MC error" criterion:

  true squared Mahalanobis target : 3.728339
  NULL    mean = +0.003071  MC se = 0.004899  z = +0.63
  SIGNAL  mean = +3.714054  MC se = 0.020777  bias = -0.014284  z = -0.69
  prespecified 3-sigma tolerances at nrep=400: null |mean| < 0.01470, signal |mean-target| < 0.06233
  MC se ~ 1/sqrt(nrep): 0.0098 at 100 reps, 0.0031 at 1000

Most useful bit: the criterion discriminates hard. The same simulation with a NON-crossvalidated estimator gives null mean +1.9725 instead of 0, about 400 MC standard errors off. So the test would instantly catch an implementation that stopped cross-validating - which is what makes it worth writing rather than a formality.

Assert both arms: null centering is the sensitive one, signal recovery rules out a correctly-centered but wrongly-scaled estimator. Full numbers in the decision note on Epic 6, reproducible with set.seed(2026).
